items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: At the Downbeat, I had Russell Jack, Eleanor's brother, was playing trumpet

ctx.x: I had a couple of bands at the Downbeat, and I don't know which came first. At one time, I had Marshall Royal, and yeah ... that came later; this is about right.

At the Downbeat, I had Russell Jack, Eleanor's brother, was playing trumpet; marvelous pianist -- what was that guy's name? I can see him, but ... really good pianist, and Charlie Mingus was playing bass with me. At the Downbeat. What happened is Johnny Otis was at the Club Alabam, which was 3 doors down, so Stan Kenton -- and I have it in right order -- Stan Kenton came on the Avenue because he was looking for a drummer, and someone told him to come hear Johnny Otis. Okay.

So he went in and he heard Johnny, and he just happened to stop in the Downbeat. He stopped in the Downbeat and he heard me, you know. I was his man. He was -- he wanted me and I was gonna join Stan's band; as a matter of fact, I've always been a 'word' man, and it was kind of embarrassing that I went back on my word. We negotiated the salary, you know, and we got up to like $350 -- and $350 then was a lot of money, you know? Because I didn't want to leave home ... because I didn't want to leave home because of…
